speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly how your cough feels, and does it produce any mucus? If so, what color is the mucus and how much do you cough up? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation with flattened diaphragms, increased retrosternal airspace and a prominent hilar shadow suggestive of emphysema.

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray strongly suggests emphysema. Have you ever been diagnosed with chronic bronchitis or asthma, and do you have a significant history of smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I have a significant history of smoking, having worked as a construction worker and smoking for decades before quitting five years ago. Additionally, I was diagnosed with chronic bronchitis several years ago, which has made this recent worsening of my cough and breathlessness quite concerning. However, hospital policy during the current surge is to avoid non-essential labs. Cardiac diagnosis must be made from clinical evaluation only.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history combined with the X-ray findings is highly suggestive of COPD, but I need to distinguish if there is an acute exacerbation or if heart failure is contributing given your shortness of breath. Have you noticed swelling in your legs, or does your cough worsen significantly in the morning?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with Emphysema and Chronic Bronchitis
